Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Vivek Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri R.P. Patel, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.182 of 2016, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C.,
Police Station Shikohabad, District Firozabad, during the pendency of trial.

4. As per prosecution case, the date of birth of the applicant is stated to be 17.12.1995, and subsequent to it, the applicant is stated to have got the admission form in the high-school filled up by reducing age three years and showing it to be 17.12.1998 in order to claim juvenility in Case Puneet Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161724475/
1 Crime No.252 of 2015, in which he is languishing in jail.

entities.text: Case Puneet Kumar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
The applicant has passed his high-school examination in the year 2013.

The applicant is in jail since 17.8.2016 in the present case and in Case Crime No.252 of 2015 he went to jail in the year 2015 itself, as such there was no question of applicant forging the documents well before the incident.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence.
There is no other criminal antecedent of the applicant except one case in which he is languishing in jail.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

7. In the case of Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2020 (11) SCC 648, the Apex Court has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail, if otherwise his case of bail is made out.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2020 (11) SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant- Puneet Kumar, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
11.

It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
